This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award dated 01.03.2024 passed in MVC NO.346/2022 on the file of the court of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Belur, Hassan, for enhancing the compensation.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Belur, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Learned counsel for appellant remained absent on 05.03.2026.
Even today he did not turn up.
The NC: 2026:KHC:13835 HC-KAR ranks of the parties are retained as per tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. One Chethan @ Chethankumar, son of Devaraju met with an accident on 17.10.2021 and his parents and sister filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.
Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of Rs.21,81,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from date of petition till realisation.
4. Aggrieved by the said order, they preferred an appeal and mainly contended that Chethan was earning Rs.30,000/- per month by doing agriculture work and social work.
But the Tribunal has considered his income as Rs.15,000/- which is on lower side.
Ex.P10 was not considered and also submits that 1/3rd deduction towards personal expenses is on higher side.
The Tribunal ought to have considered Ex.P10 while assessing the income and 50% deduction is on higher side.
More compensation NC: 2026:KHC:13835 HC-KAR ought to have been granted under loss of future prospects.
Thus, requested for enhancement of the compensation.

2 5.
Learned Counsel of the respondent stated that Ex.P10 is only letter issued by the Taluka Panchayath, but the author of Exhibit P10 was not examined and thus notional income was rightly considered.
However, on the perusal of the record it shows that he has not filed any income proof.

As he met with accident in 2021, based on the chart as per Karnataka State Legal Services authority,
the Tribunal has rightly considered the notional income as Rs.15,000/- and he was aged 32 years and the multiplier is taken as 16 and he is entitled for 40% towards future prospects and 50% is to be deducted towards personal expenses.
The total loss of dependency was rightly calculated by the tribunal as Rs.20,16,000/.
The tribunal also rightly granted the amount under the head consortium and conventional heads and arrived to the final figure of Rs.21,81,000/-.
Tribunal rightly considered all the aspects and granted reasonable amount.
But the claimant NC: 2026:KHC:13835 HC-KAR preferred appeal and not turned up and not made any representation.
Therefore, this Court finds there are no merits in the appeal.
Accordingly, appeal is dismissed confirming the order of the tribunal.
Insurance company already deposited the entire amount.
Therefore, claimants are permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued as per the apportionment of the tribunal.

Sd/-
